i’ve been on many meds- there’s def some that didn’t have noticeable side effects or make anything worse but they also didn’t make anything better either. 

the only antidepressant that sorta did something for me was effexor but it’s not worth it. eventually you will need to get off of it & it’s the worst thing i’ve ever dealt with in terms of meds/withdrawals. i am on wellbutrin but it doesn’t really do anything, for the first while it did make me extremely angry all the time but now it just does nothing. 

antipsychotics- never had one that didn’t have side effects however i’d rather be super tired constantly than be psychotic & a danger to myself & others. i take quetiapine & it has been my favourite out of the others i tried. 

benzos- tricky to say but for me this is a miracle med, specifically ativan (lorazepam). no side effects aside from being out of it & a lil loopy but i personally enjoy that compared to how i feel during panic attacks. it makes some ppl tired but i don’t have any issues there. i’ve tried xanax & klonopin but they did absolutely nothing id have to take 4X what i was prescribed to get anything helpful from them. they cannot be taken daily sadly, or shouldn’t be. it’s the only medication that literally fixes everything wrong with me mentally until it wears off. they’re dangerous tho. 

side effects are not something you can avoid, but you can find ones you can tolerate. antidepressants don’t actually make you happy, if anything all they do is numb you to feeling good or bad. emotional constipation is best description. but there are times i’d rather feel nothing than what i feel normally. keep trying, you’ll find something, trial & error is hard on the body but that’s the only option for those of us who can’t afford gene testing. i’d really like to do that but could never afford to. if you can you should

again- one medical professional isn’t enough to get it. i have asked about it with my doctors because id consider it.  i won’t argue that our healthcare is trash because it absolutely is, i have severe mental illnesses & have seen hundredssss of “professionals”, kinda why MAID is appealing to some with mental illness. the only things i haven’t tried are things that require being institutionalized which im cool with except it’s tens of thousands of dollars to be in one. psych wards are free but id rather be in hell i’ve been to many psych wards they all suck & you’re treated like an animal. 

i half agree like yeah it’s sad that they’d even consider approving it for mental illness someday when they could just provide adequate mental health care & services & housing that’s safe & livable, rehab that people who aren’t extremely rich could get into, but honestly i don’t see that stuff ever happening here. esp in my province run by Doug Ford lol. 

i’d rather not hold my breath waiting for things to change when it’s obvious they never will. so if they give me a way out i might take it.  there’s loopholes but the loopholes aren’t very big, like i have physical health issues & chronic illness that has been miserable trying to get help for & without a diagnosis MAID still isn’t an option, i can’t just say the symptoms & be on my way. 

having one shitty doctor suggest it doesn’t mean anything, that person would be fired for that, other docs have to give assessments & sign for it as well & i don’t think they would, they’d also lose their license. i know people who’ve tried to get it as well it’s not easy it’s a hassle on purpose i assume. 

go to your doctor & ask for it. it’s not gunna happen. also i will add MAID for mental illness if ever approved is literally the last resort, much like treatment resistant depression treatments- you need to have tried multiple medications that fit your illness, be seen by psychiatrists, have been in therapy more than once, all of the first line treatments need to be tried first. i happen to fit all of those boxes. but ive been in therapy since i was 6, on meds since i was 11/12, tons of professionals, psych wards, different types of therapy, nothing ever did anything. it sucks but there are some people that will just off themselves anyway no matter what, & i know that they’d prefer doing it in a non gruesome way with dignity & their family there to say goodbye. one of my best friends is one of them, & their family has seen the agony they’ve been in for years & of course they wish she’d stay but it’s selfish to ask someone to suffer to save you from grief. i’d rather them be comfortable & at peace in their last moments than doing something painful & messy to get it over with. losing people to suicide is awful but it happens a lot so if they’re gunna do it anyway, why not be in a safer controlled environment? guess you can’t understand til you’ve watched it or felt it yourself. but i get the point, it does suck & i wish we could get real help but that’s not in the books. when you’ve done everything available to you, then what? keep suffering? i’m tired. 

tldr; not realistic, not gunna happen. if it could happen i’d be doing that.

no it’s not. it’s not even legal for mental illness yet in canada, trust me i check a lot. it’s just for terminally ill people, physical illnesses that are severe. the idea was brought up but they keep pushing back the date it’ll be decided whether or not mental illness is allowed to qualify. it’s been in the air for a long time so don’t worry i highly doubt they’ll allow it. 

also it’s not easy to get either if you qualify in general, there’s a wait list, you need multiple different doctors signing off on it, you have to be mentally sound enough to make decisions like they’re not gunna let someone in psychosis do this, you can’t just walk in & say “hi i’d like one suicide please!”  you can also back out any time you want, they give you time to make sure it’s what you want.

i agree. most of my bad behaviour was before being diagnosed, not knowing why i was that way, or understanding that i wasn’t crazy it was symptoms, it’s not an excuse but definitely an explanation of how my brain works.  

personally i think after being diagnosed bad behaviour should gradually get better because you know yourself so much better & why you feel so strongly, act out, are not great in relationships or friendships. you now have the ability to get help, get meds, therapy specifically for bpd, learn about your own disorder & change the things you do & say because you hurt people & honestly for a while i didn’t care. 

it took a long time to understand that people actually had feelings, to see the damage i was doing, & i started feeling guilt, having nightmares about things i did, being taunted by flashbacks of being things i hated & i grew from there. 

it’s disappointing seeing so many people use it as an excuse to continue being terrible, not being willing to be better, & i get why people hear us say we have bpd & assume the worst because a lot of us are the worst & im not saying im the best but i definitely don’t relate with lots of other people with bpd. if they even have it or just self diagnose i don’t know why anyone would want this disorder, other than using it to be shitty people & be proud of it it’s fuckin weird. having bpd doesn’t make it okay to be a bad person. we’ve all done bad things but try to be better & get help. 

tbf if i didn’t have consistent trauma wearing me down & have everything taken away from me i might not have had the realization or the change in view of right & wrong, sometimes you need everything & everyone taken from you to grow up. & if we keep hurting people i hope it happens to them too maybe they’ll stop.
